title: Evaluating LLM Generated Detection Rules in Cybersecurity
abstract: arXiv:2509.16749v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLMs are increasingly pervasive in the security environment, with limited measures of their effectiveness, which limits trust and usefulness to security practitioners. Here, we present an open-source evaluation framework and benchmark metrics for evaluating LLM-generated cybersecurity rules. The benchmark employs a holdout set-based methodology to measure the effectiveness of LLM-generated security rules in comparison to a human-generated corpus of rules. It provides three key metrics inspired by the way experts evaluate security rules, offering a realistic, multifaceted evaluation of the effectiveness of an LLM-based security rule generator. This methodology is illustrated using rules from Sublime Security's detection team and those written by Sublime Security's Automated Detection Engineer (ADE), with a thorough analysis of ADE's skills presented in the results section.

translated_title: 评估网络安全中LLM生成的检测规则
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在安全环境中的应用日益广泛，但其有效性缺乏衡量手段，这限制了安全从业者对其的信任和实用性。为此，我们提出一个开源评估框架和基准指标，用于评估LLM生成的网络安全规则。该基准采用基于留出集的方法，将LLM生成的安全规则与人工生成的规则语料库进行比较，以衡量其有效性。它提供了三个关键指标，灵感来源于专家评估安全规则的方式，从而对基于LLM的安全规则生成器的有效性进行现实且多方面的评估。该方法的示例使用了Sublime Security检测团队编写的规则以及Sublime Security自动化检测工程师（ADE）编写的规则，结果部分对ADE的技能进行了深入分析。
tldr: 本文提出了一种开源评估框架和基准指标，用于客观衡量LLM生成的网络安全检测规则的有效性，并通过留出集方法及专家启发的多维指标与人工规则对比，为安全领域提供可信的评估工具。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an open-source evaluation framework and benchmark metrics to objectively assess the effectiveness of LLM-generated cybersecurity detection rules, comparing them against human-crafted rules via holdout sets and expert-inspired multifaceted metrics.
